title: Strategies — the roster and what each one governs

data.name: listings
data.shape: StrategyListing[] — { strategy, governs, editable, fork: {kind:'offered'} | {kind:'withheld', because} }

components.purpose: Show every strategy the user can reach and, for each, how many agents it currently governs.

actions.effect: The strategy's name links to /strategies/<id> — the detail page (exists since get_strategy landed)

components.current_implementation: Bordered ul of li, styled with Tailwind (3.4.19, installed since this surface was first surveyed — the classes now render). The `empty` branch exists now and is its own render, not a length check: it says nothing is listed — not even BattleGrid's own catalog — and deliberately offers no next action, because an empty result means there is nothing to fork from either. (`strategy-list-has-no-empty-state` is closed.) The unreadable branch is role=alert with a heading, the raw reason, and the why-not-loaded sentence. | strategy-row: Bordered li; name (an underlined link to the strategy detail page) and a scope/revision caption on one baseline row, optional tagline, then the governs line. No truncation handling for long names or taglines. | fork-capacity-notice: role=status bordered paragraph above the list. | fork-withheld: the row renders the reason (fork.because) as plain secondary text in the actions list, where the fork control would have been.
constraints: The bound-agent count ('governs') must stay visible on the roster row itself, not behind a hover or a detail click — a strategy is never an isolated object here, and the count belongs where the user first meets it rather than only in the confirmation, by which point they have already decided

`unreadable` must keep saying the strategies are not gone. *Why* they could not be shown now varies by cause and must keep varying — a platform that refused is not a platform that could not be reached, and the distinction between 'you have none', 'we were refused' and 'we could not ask' must survive any redesign
Rows with boundAgentCount > 0 are currently emphasised relative to zero-bound rows; that difference must remain perceivable without relying on font-weight alone

[strategy-row] 'BattleGrid' vs 'Yours' (scope) must remain distinguishable at a glance — it decides whether the row offers Edit or Fork, and a user who misreads it will try an action the platform refuses
[strategy-row] Revision number must stay attached to the strategy it belongs to; it is the identity users track across edits
[strategy-row] Long names and taglines must not push the actions out of reach — currently untested and unhandled
[fork-capacity-notice] Must stay non-blocking — it explains a limit, it does not stop the user browsing or editing what they already have
[fork-capacity-notice] Announced via role=status; it appears without a user action and must not steal focus

`empty` is a third branch, distinct from both `default` and `unreadable`, and it offers no action on purpose. `list_strategies` returns BattleGrid's visible catalog alongside the user's own, so an empty result means there is nothing to fork from — a 'start by forking one of BattleGrid's' affordance would point at something that was not returned, and would read as reassurance

[strategy-row] The name must remain the link to the strategy itself — every row once offered four verbs and no way to look at the thing they act on. The name holds the noun; the actions list holds the verbs

[strategy-row] A withheld fork must render its reason in the row, where the control would have been — not only as a page-level notice. Twelve rows each saying why read as a screen that knows why it is offering nothing; twelve bare gaps read as one that forgot

components.purpose: Tell a user their work still exists, and say accurately why it could not be shown.
components.current_implementation:
One

inside the unreadable branch of both the roster and the strategy list. The reassurance clause is fixed and outside the conditional; only the cause clause varies. Takes a `subject` string so the two callers share one sentence rather than holding two copies.
constraints: The reassurance ('this does not mean X are gone') must render in BOTH states. It is the only thing on screen telling a user their work still exists, and it sits outside the branch so neither case can be written without it

`refused` and `unreachable` must not be collapsed back into one sentence. A refusal means BattleGrid was reached and declined — waiting changes nothing and the credential is the fix. Unreachable means no usable answer came back — the credential may be fine and waiting may be exactly right. Naming the wrong one sends a user to wait for an outage that is not happening

Neither state may be softened into a vague 'something went wrong'. The sentence earns its reassurance by naming a cause that is obviously external and obviously not deletion; a vaguer cause is a weaker reassurance
The cause arrives as a value on the result. Nothing here may re-derive it by matching on the reason text

components.purpose: Turn away a request that has no authority, and say how to fix it.
components.current_implementation: Shared component rendered in place of the page body. Reachable only on a delegated deployment: a personal one resolves the acting user from a configured key and never returns not-connected, so this page cannot render there.
constraints: Every cause — no session, forged cookie, unknown user, revoked connection, unrefreshable token, 401 from BattleGrid — arrives here and must keep producing one page. They differ in cause and not in remedy, and splitting them visually would imply actions the user does not have (design W-C)
Must not imply the user's data is lost

flows.name: Fork a platform strategy to edit it
steps: Make my own copy to edit

accessibility.notes: Per-row nav is labelled `Actions for <strategy name>`. Load failure is role=alert; fork capacity is role=status. No live region for the list itself — it is server-rendered and does not update in place.
